title: Margin Dynamics for Large Language Model Alignment
claim: Alignment methods differ along three axes, repulsion, margin growth and reference handling, which determine whether training pressure fades, diverges or stays stable.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right; simplex vector fields, then two dynamics curve plots
description: Three labeled panels, each covering one axis of the framework. Panel (a), Repulsion, shows two triangles (simplices) with vertices y_w at the top and y_l1 and y_l2 at the bottom. In the SFT triangle, green arrows point up toward y_w and fade as they approach the apex. An arrow leads to the DPO triangle, where blue arrows near the apex and red arrows along the sides show sustained flow. A legend marks F+ in blue and F- in red, with captions 'F+ only: fades' and 'F+ - F-: sustained'. Panel (b), Margin, plots Δ against t. The DPO curve (blue) keeps growing, PPO (lavender) grows more slowly, and IPO (red) flattens at the dashed line 1/(2τ). Panel (c), Reference, plots gradient norm against t. The Frozen curve (blue) decays, None (purple) drifts upward, and Adaptive (salmon) stays flat. Short captions sit under each plot.
caption: Three axes of the margin dynamics framework. (a) SFT only attracts toward $y_w$ ($F^+$), with pressure vanishing as $\pi(y_l) \to 0$. DPO adds targeted repulsion $F^-$, sustaining $\Omega(\pi)$ pressure. (b) Sigmoid weighting (DPO) yields unbounded margin growth; linear weighting (IPO, PPO) converges. (c) Frozen references cause gradient decay; reference-free methods risk drift; adaptive references stay stable.
abstract: Practitioners choose among LLM alignment methods largely by trial and error. We provide a theoretical foundation: each pairwise method defines a vector field on the probability simplex that governs how the model redistributes mass between preferred and dispreferred completions. Projecting onto a single preferred/dispreferred pair reduces this to a one-dimensional margin ODE with a closed-form solution. These solutions reveal that DPO margins grow without bound (logarithmically as $O(\log t)$ in the gradient-flow limit) while IPO margins converge to a finite $1/(2Ï)$; that label noise induces a qualitative phase transition in DPO (unbounded $\to$ bounded) but affects IPO only quantitatively; and that gradient concentration under asymmetric weighting governs trainability at scale. We confirm all three predictions across five model families spanning four benchmarks. The closed-form solutions also enable principled method design: we prove that adding any label smoothing $\varepsilon > 0$ to SimPO creates a finite margin attractor at $Î^* = Î²^{-1}\log((1-\varepsilon)/\varepsilon)$, while $\varepsilon = 0$ (standard SimPO) has no attractor. We test this across three models (8B-9B) and confirm the prediction: the theory-derived configuration (TPO-S, $\varepsilon = 0.05$) is competitive with the strongest baselines, attaining the highest mean IFEval score among the compared methods on all three, validating that the predicted finite attractor is a usable operating point rather than proposing a new state-of-the-art loss.
